small_guidance:
- Sweep TILE_W ∈ {8, 16, 32} with num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8} via triton.autotune; current Wp is small (likely 16 or 17), so TILE_W=16 with num_warps=2 may reduce per-program overhead and increase grid parallelism.
- Hoist the bias load (`bv`) out of the (ddp,dhp,dwp) loop — bias is invariant across the 8 pool positions, so add it once after the gemm loop or fold into the final cmax compare.
- Try reordering the IC loop as the innermost dimension and pre-loading the weight slab `wv[OC, IC]` per (kd,kh,kw) once (independent of offs_t) so the inner offs_t loop only does input gathers; this reduces redundant weight loads by TILE_W×.
large_guidance:
- Switch from gather-style transposed conv to a scatter-add im2col GEMM: for each input voxel, compute the OC×(KD·KH·KW) contribution and scatter into a pre-conv buffer; then a separate fused kernel does maxpool+softmax+sub+swish+channel-max. The current kernel re-computes validity masks and reloads weights for every output tile, which is the main inefficiency.
- Alternatively, restructure as one program per (N, dp, hp) covering the entire Wp row and all 8 pool sub-positions, keeping the OC×Wp accumulator persistent and looping kd/kh/kw with weights staged in shared memory. This amortizes weight loads across the whole row and removes the Wp_tiles dimension.
- Consider a two-stage design: (1) Triton transposed-conv writing (N, OC, Dout, Hout, Wout) in channels-last, (2) a single fused kernel doing maxpool3d + channelwise softmax + subtract + swish + channel-max in one pass over the conv output. This decouples the heavy GEMM from the small fused tail and lets each be tuned independently.
